newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fernz expects investment grade S&P rating.
newsitem.headline: Fernz expects investment grade S&P rating.

text.p: Fernz Corp Ltd Chairman Bill Wilson said the company expected an investment grade rating from Standard and Poor's after discussions with the ratings agency.
Wilson, responding to a question at the annual meeting about the company's planned NZ$150 million capital notes programme, said he expected Fernz to attain investment grade by November.
Shareholders voted on a proposal to change the company's constitution by replacing the current "notice and pause" takeover provision with the more restrictive "minority veto".
A result is expected later today.

Minority veto means all shareholders must be made the same takeover offer price in a takeover. It requires five days' notice for an on market bid and 15 days for an off market bid, the longest of all takeover provisions.
Wilson said the directors had had a change of heart since the last annual meeting, which adopted the standard notice and pause provision.
Minority veto, he said, would allow a fairer deal for all shareholders if a bid were made for the company.
